rationale: C14 is an unmistakable drafting template. The child repeats its two-paragraph structure and nearly all operative language verbatim, changing only the designated agencies and the effective accrual date. C18 is contextually related because it created and empowered one of the newly designated agencies, but it does not supply the child's designation-and-contract-applicability formula. C08 has a superficially similar agency-designation mechanism but lacks the distinctive two-step structure and language shared with C14.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Defense Materials Procurement Agency, the Bureau of Mines, and the (United States) Geological Survey, each of which exercises functions having a direct and immediate connection with the national defense, are hereby designated, pursuant to section 103(a) of the Act, as agencies of the Government included within the definition of the term "Department" for the purposes of Title I of the Act.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Federal Civil Defense Administration, the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics, the Tennessee Valley Authority, and the United State Coast Guard, each of which exercises functions having a direct and immediate connection with the national defense, and hereby designated, pursuant to section 103 (a) of the Act, as agencies of the Government included within the definition of the term "Department" for the purposes of Title I of the Act.
shared_material.explanation: The same distinctive statutory designation formula is reused, with only the agency list changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In accordance with section 102 of the Act, the provisions of Title I of the Act shall be applicable to all contracts with the Defense Materials Procurement Agency, the Bureau of Mines, and the (United States) Geological Survey, respectively, and related subcontracts, to the extent of the amounts received or accrued by a contractor or subcontractor on or after the first day of October 1951, whether such contracts or subcontracts were made on, before, or after that date.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In accordance with section 102 of the Act, the provisions of Title I of the Act, shall be applicable to all contracts with each agency designated in paragraph 1 of this order, and related subcontracts, to the extent of the amounts received or accrued by a contractor or subcontractor on or after the first day of July 1951, whether such contracts or subcontracts were made on, before, or after that date.
shared_material.explanation: The child follows the same second-step contract and subcontract applicability provision, including the distinctive accrual rule and retroactive coverage formulation, while substituting the agencies and effective date.
